Status of this draft: The decisions DEC-001 to DEC-014 were taken by the designer on 2026-10-25.
The decisions DEC-015 to DEC-028 are choices of the author of this draft that the designer has not yet confirmed (Section 20); the RTL in rtl/ was written with them as stated.

The SDC file constraints/m_vlsit_apbcdc_top.sdc was executed only with stub commands (constraints/check_sdc.py); it was not run in a sign-off tool (open item OI-004).

The IP carries one AMBA APB transfer at a time from an APB requester in clock domain MST to an APB completer in clock domain SLV.
The two clocks are asynchronous to each other: any frequency ratio and any phase (DEC-008).

The bridge is an APB completer on its requester-side interface and an APB requester on its completer-side interface; the two interfaces are named by the clock domain suffix mst and slv (DEC-001, rule PRT-02).
APB allows only one transfer in flight, so the bridge is not a FIFO: a handshake with bundled data crosses the domains (DEC-002).

The requester-side logic captures the request fields once, in the Setup phase, into a hold register and launches a request bit; the completer-side logic sees the request after a synchronizer, loads the fields into its own register, runs one normal APB transfer, holds the response, and returns an acknowledge bit; the requester-side logic sees the acknowledge after a synchronizer and returns the response.
Only the one-bit request, acknowledge and wake-up signals pass through synchronizers.

The multi-bit request and response bundles are never sampled by a synchronizer: they are held stable for the whole handshake and loaded by the destination only after the control bit has arrived, and the timing of these bundle paths is bounded by set_max_delay constraints (Section 17).
The handshake is selectable: a two-phase (toggle) handshake or a four-phase (level) handshake (parameter PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE, DEC-005).
The interface is APB4 or APB5 (parameter PARA_APBCDC_APB5, DEC-003).
Included:
APB4 transfers: PSEL, PENABLE, PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB, PWDATA, PREADY, PRDATA, PSLVERR, with wait states and error responses.
APB5 option: PWAKEUP, and the user signals PAUSER, PWUSER, PRUSER, PBUSER with configurable widths (width 0 = signal not present).
Two-phase and four-phase handshake, selectable at elaboration.
Synchronizer depth selectable at elaboration with the cell option of 001_AsyncGrayFIFO (PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE).
Complete SDC for the crossing paths and the interfaces (Synopsys dialect, DEC-007).
Excluded:
Parity protection and the check signals of APB5 (DEC-003).
Several completers: one PSEL on the completer side, no address decode (DEC-013).
Timeout on the completer side: the bridge waits for PREADY without limit (DEC-006).
Software-visible registers, interrupts, DFT structures, security and safety functions, clock gating, power domains.
Verification-only models and testbenches (verification source set).

This specification and the decisions of Section 20 define the behavior of the IP.
REF-001 is the authority for APB.
Where this specification restates an APB rule, REF-001 wins; a conflict is recorded as an open item.
REF-003 is the mandatory RTL coding, hierarchy, reset, CDC and naming baseline.
A conflict is resolved by revising the requirement or choosing a compliant implementation, not by a local RTL exception.
The one recorded deviation is DEC-021.
The IP has no registers, so there is no CSR workbook.
Conflicts are resolved through an explicit decision recorded in Section 20.

Naming rule: the default naming rule of vlsit-rtl-generator, section 2 of VLSIT_RTL_Design_Rule.md v2 (clauses NAM-01 to NAM-09 and PRT-01 to PRT-04), path VLSIT_RTL_Generator_AI_Model\spec_template\VLSIT_RTL_Design_Rule.md, version v2, chosen by the designer on 2026-10-25 (answer 1A, rule R-026, DEC-001).

Protocol ports follow PRT-01: the form is the direction prefix i or o at the boundary of the module, then apb, then the lowercase APB mnemonic; the two APB interfaces are told apart by the direction prefix and by their clock domain (i_apb_psel is the requester-side input, o_apb_psel the completer-side output).

Standard: AMBA APB; Revision / profile: Issue D, APB4 profile (PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 0) and APB5 profile (PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1); Role implemented: Completer on the requester-side interface, requester on the completer-side interface; Options: PSTRB, PPROT, PSLVERR always present; APB5: PWAKEUP, PAUSER, PWUSER, PRUSER, PBUSER; Deviations: No parity check signals (DEC-003). PSLVERR of a completer that does not drive it is tied low outside the IP

ID: REQ-FUNC-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: For every APB transfer that the requester starts on the requester-side interface, the bridge shall start exactly one APB transfer on the completer-side interface with the same PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB, and, for a write, the same PWDATA; in APB5 also the same PAUSER and, for a write, the same PWUSER. The values are those driven in the Setup phase.; Source: DEC-002, REF-001 3.1, 3.3; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Scoreboard simulation: TEST-002, TEST-003, TEST-011; assertion SVA-008; waveform WF-001, WF-002

ID: REQ-FUNC-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall return on the requester-side interface the response of the completer-side transfer unchanged: PRDATA of a read, PSLVERR, and in APB5 PRUSER of a read and PBUSER. The response values are valid in the cycle where PREADY is high.; Source: DEC-002, REF-001 3.3, 3.4, Appendix A; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Scoreboard simulation: TEST-003, TEST-005; assertion SVA-004; waveform WF-002, WF-004

ID: REQ-FUNC-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The transfers shall be carried in the order in which they start, one completer-side transfer per requester-side transfer, with no loss, no duplicate, and no new completer-side transfer before the response of the previous one was delivered.; Source: DEC-002; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Scoreboard simulation: TEST-002, TEST-011; assertions SVA-009, SVA-010

ID: REQ-FUNC-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: PREADY on the requester-side interface shall be low from the Setup phase until the response is available, and shall then be high for exactly one cycle of i_clk_mst, in a cycle in which PSEL and PENABLE are high.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 4.1; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002; assertions SVA-001, SVA-002; waveform WF-001

ID: REQ-FUNC-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: Wait states of the completer shall extend the requester-side transfer: the requester-side PREADY is raised only after the completer-side PREADY was seen. The bridge shall wait without limit (no timeout, DEC-006).; Source: DEC-006, REF-001 3.1; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-004; waveform WF-003

ID: REQ-FUNC-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: PSLVERR on the requester-side interface shall be high only in the PREADY cycle, and only when the completer-side PSLVERR was high at the end of the completer-side transfer.; Source: REF-001 3.4; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-005; assertion SVA-003; waveform WF-004, WF-005

ID: REQ-FUNC-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall accept the Setup phase of a new requester-side transfer in the cycle that follows the PREADY cycle (back-to-back transfer, Figure 4-1 of REF-001).; Source: REF-001 4.1; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; waveform WF-006

ID: REQ-FUNC-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: On the completer-side interface the bridge shall drive PSEL high for the whole transfer, PENABLE low in the Setup cycle and high from the next cycle until the transfer completes, keep PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PAUSER, PWUSER unchanged from the Setup phase until PREADY is seen high, and drive PSEL and PENABLE low when no transfer is in progress.; Source: REF-001 3.1, 4.1; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-013; assertions SVA-005, SVA-006, SVA-007

ID: REQ-FUNC-009; Requirement using shall/should/may: PPROT and PSTRB shall be forwarded unchanged. The bridge does not check the rule that PSTRB is low in a read; it forwards what the requester drove.; Source: REF-001 3.2, 3.5, DEC-028; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-007; waveform WF-008

ID: REQ-IF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall expose exactly the ports of Section 6.2 of the configured revision.; Source: REF-003 PRT-03, DEC-021; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Lint and port-list review: TEST-015

ID: REQ-IF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: Every output of both APB interfaces shall be the output of a flip-flop with no logic after it, so that it is glitch-free (REF-001 3.6 requires this for PWAKEUP).; Source: DEC-019, REF-001 3.6; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Structural check of the RTL and the netlist: TEST-015

ID: REQ-IF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: Outputs that need not be valid shall hold a stable value (reset value zero). PRDATA, PRUSER, PBUSER are valid with PREADY; PSLVERR is low when PREADY is low.; Source: REF-001 Appendix A, DEC-024; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-001, TEST-013; assertion SVA-017

ID: REQ-HS-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE = 0 selects the two-phase handshake: the request bit toggles once per transfer and the acknowledge bit toggles once per transfer. PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE = 1 selects the four-phase handshake: request high, acknowledge high, request low, acknowledge low. The function seen on the two APB interfaces shall be the same.; Source: DEC-005; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-008; assertions SVA-012, SVA-013; waveform WF-001, WF-007

ID: REQ-HS-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The request bundle in the requester-side hold register shall not change from the edge that launches the request until the acknowledge was seen, and the response bundle in the completer-side hold register shall not change from the edge that launches the acknowledge until the next request was seen.; Source: DEC-002, DEC-023; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Assertion SVA-011; simulation: TEST-002

ID: REQ-HS-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The request bit shall be launched at the same clock edge at which the request bundle is loaded, and the acknowledge bit at the same edge at which the response bundle is loaded; between a launch flip-flop and its synchronizer there shall be no logic.; Source: DEC-016, REF-003 CLK-01, P28; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Structural check: TEST-015; STA review: TEST-016

ID: REQ-HS-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: With the four-phase handshake the requester side shall raise PREADY only after the acknowledge returned to 0, so that the handshake is closed before the next Setup phase can be accepted.; Source: DEC-020; Applies to: CFG-4PH; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-008; assertion SVA-013; waveform WF-007

ID: REQ-CLK-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall be correct for any frequency ratio and any phase of i_clk_mst and i_clk_slv, equal frequency included.; Source: DEC-008; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation with many ratios: TEST-011

ID: REQ-CLK-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: Only the five crossings of Section 7.2 shall exist between the domains: request, request bundle, acknowledge, response bundle, and wake-up. Each control bit shall cross through a synchronizer and no bundle bit shall cross through one.; Source: DEC-002, REF-003 CLK-01; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Structural check: TEST-015

ID: REQ-CLK-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The synchronizer depth shall follow PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE (1 and 2: two stages, 3: three stages, 4: four stages). The value 0 (no stage) is for simulation only and shall not be used in a netlist; the SDC rejects it.; Source: DEC-026, REF-005; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Elaboration and SDC check: TEST-014, TEST-016

ID: REQ-RESET-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: Both resets shall be active-low with asynchronous assertion. While one is asserted, every flip-flop of its domain shall be at its reset value: all payload registers 0, request 0, acknowledge 0, both FSMs in IDLE, PSEL, PENABLE, PREADY, PSLVERR, PWAKEUP 0.; Source: REF-003 RST-01, DEC-009; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Reset test: TEST-001; assertion SVA-016

ID: REQ-RESET-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The two resets shall be asserted together and each shall be released synchronously to the clock of its domain, outside the IP. A transfer in flight when a reset is asserted is lost. Asserting only one reset is not supported.; Source: DEC-009; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-012; waveform WF-012

ID: REQ-APB5-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: In APB5, o_apb_pwakeup shall be a flip-flop output that is high whenever the synchronized i_apb_pwakeup is high or a transfer is in progress on the completer side, and shall be high no later than o_apb_psel.; Source: DEC-010, REF-001 3.6; Applies to: CFG-APB5; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009; assertions SVA-014, SVA-015; waveform WF-009

ID: REQ-APB5-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: In APB5, PAUSER, PWUSER, PRUSER, PBUSER shall be transported with the same timing rules as the other request and response fields; a signal whose width parameter is 0 is not present.; Source: DEC-003, REF-001 3.7; Applies to: CFG-APB5, CFG-USER; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-010; waveform WF-009

ID: REQ-APB5-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: With PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 0 the APB5 signals shall have no effect: o_apb_pwakeup is 0 and the user outputs are 0.; Source: DEC-003, DEC-021; Applies to: CFG-APB4; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-009

ID: REQ-PARAM-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall accept the parameter values of Section 8. The behavior with an illegal value is not specified and the IP does not check it.; Source: DEC-004; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Elaboration of the legal extremes: TEST-014

ID: REQ-PERF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: With the two-phase handshake, the duration from the first cycle of the Setup phase to the end of the PREADY cycle on the requester side shall not exceed (N + 3) x T_mst + (N + 3 + w) x T_slv, where N is the number of synchronizer stages, w the number of completer wait states, and T the clock periods.; Source: DEC-005, DEC-016; Applies to: All configurations with HS_TYPE 0; Verification method: Latency sweep: TEST-018; waveform WF-001, WF-010, WF-011

ID: REQ-PERF-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: With the four-phase handshake the same duration shall not exceed (2N + 4) x T_mst + (2N + 4 + w) x T_slv.; Source: DEC-005, DEC-020; Applies to: All configurations with HS_TYPE 1; Verification method: Latency sweep: TEST-018; waveform WF-007

ID: REQ-PERF-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The bridge shall carry one transfer at a time and shall accept the next Setup phase in the cycle after the PREADY cycle.; Source: DEC-013; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-006; waveform WF-006

ID: REQ-TIM-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall be delivered with an SDC file in the Synopsys dialect that defines the two clocks, the interface budgets, and the exceptions of the five crossings, with the budgets computed from the clock periods and the synchronizer depth.; Source: DEC-007; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: SDC execution check: TEST-016

ID: REQ-TIM-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: Each crossing path shall be constrained by set_max_delay with the clock latency ignored; no set_clock_groups -asynchronous and no set_false_path (other than the hold-only false path of the crossings) shall exist between the two clocks.; Source: DEC-018, DEC-017; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: SDC review in the sign-off tool: TEST-016

ID: REQ-TIM-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: After clock-tree synthesis the difference between the clock latencies of the launch and the capture flip-flops of every crossing shall be smaller than the guard band of one destination period used in the budget formulas.; Source: DEC-017; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Post-CTS report review: TEST-016

ID: REQ-RTL-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and shall use the hierarchy of Section 14.2.; Source: REF-003; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Lint and rule check: TEST-015

ID: REQ-RTL-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The synchronizer cells shall be instantiated only inside the wrapper m_vlsit_apbcdc_cell_sync of 000_Common/rtl_lib, named u_dont_touch_ followed by the function (REF-003 NAM-09), with a simulation model that adds a random extra latency of 0, 1 or 2 destination cycles to the output.; Source: DEC-022, REF-003 CLK-02; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Simulation: TEST-019; rule check: TEST-015

ID: REQ-VER-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: Every waveform of the plan of Section 10.3 shall exist as an image with its WaveJSON source, and the prototype scripts shall reproduce them.; Source: DEC-012; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: File check and rerun: TEST-017

ID: REQ-VER-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The random regression shall cover both handshake types, two synchronizer depths, APB4 and APB5, and at least ten clock ratios including equal clocks and a ratio of 9 to 1 in both directions, with wait states and errors, and shall report no error.; Source: DEC-008; Applies to: All configurations; Verification method: Regression: TEST-011

Illegal combinations are listed in Section 8.
The IP has two blocks, one per clock domain, and one structural top.
Each block holds one bundle register and one control flip-flop for the crossing it launches, and one synchronizer for the control bit it receives.

Block: m_vlsit_apbcdc_mst; Responsibility: APB completer of the requester: captures the Setup phase into the request hold register, launches the request bit, receives the acknowledge through the synchronizer u_sync_ack, loads the response into the response output registers and raises PREADY for one cycle; registers i_apb_pwakeup for the crossing; Inputs / outputs: Requester-side APB interface, crossing signals with the slv block; Clock/reset domain: CLK-MST / RST-MST; State or storage: reg_req_payload, reg_req, reg_wakeup, response output registers reg_resp_payload, reg_fsm_hs_current_state (IDLE, WAIT, CLOSE, RESP)

Block: m_vlsit_apbcdc_slv; Responsibility: APB requester of the completer: receives the request bit through u_sync_req and the wake-up through u_sync_wk, loads the request bundle into reg_apb_payload, drives one APB transfer, captures the response into reg_resp_hold, launches the acknowledge, and drives o_apb_pwakeup; Inputs / outputs: Completer-side APB interface, crossing signals with the mst block; Clock/reset domain: CLK-SLV / RST-SLV; State or storage: reg_apb_payload, reg_resp_hold, reg_ack, reg_fsm_hs_current_state (IDLE, SETUP, ACCESS, REQ0), reg_apb_psel, reg_apb_penable, reg_pwakeup

Block: m_vlsit_apbcdc_sync; Responsibility: Synchronizer of a vector of control bits with the cell option PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE; instantiates m_vlsit_apbcdc_cell_sync per bit; Inputs / outputs: One bit per crossing control signal; Clock/reset domain: Destination domain; State or storage: Synchronizer stages

Block: m_vlsit_apbcdc_top; Responsibility: Structural wrapper: interface, parameters, interconnect and the two instances; Inputs / outputs: All ports of Section 6.2; Clock/reset domain: CLK-MST, CLK-SLV; State or storage: None

Setup capture.

In the cycle where i_apb_psel is high and i_apb_penable is low (the Setup phase, REF-001 4.1) and the mst FSM is in IDLE, the mst block loads reg_req_payload with PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB, PWDATA and, in APB5, PAUSER, PWUSER, and launches the request: with the two-phase handshake reg_req toggles, with the four-phase handshake it rises.
All of this happens at one clock edge (DEC-016).
Request crossing. reg_req crosses through u_sync_req (N stages).
The slv FSM sees the event, loads reg_apb_payload from reg_req_payload (the bundle has been stable for at least N destination periods), raises PSEL (Setup), and one cycle later PENABLE (Access).
Completer transfer.
The slv FSM waits in ACCESS until the completer drives PREADY.
At that edge it loads reg_resp_hold with PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER, drops PSEL and PENABLE, and launches the acknowledge (toggle, or rise).
Response crossing.
The acknowledge crosses through u_sync_ack.
With the two-phase handshake the mst FSM sees the event, loads the response output registers from reg_resp_hold, and raises PREADY for one cycle (state RESP).

With the four-phase handshake the mst FSM first drops the request, waits for the acknowledge to fall (the slv FSM waits in REQ0 for the request to fall and then drops the acknowledge), and then loads the response and raises PREADY.
Next transfer.
The requester drives the next Setup phase in the cycle after the PREADY cycle; the mst FSM is back in IDLE and captures it.
Wake-up (APB5). i_apb_pwakeup is registered in the mst block, crosses through u_sync_wk, and drives o_apb_pwakeup through a flip-flop in the slv block, together with an in-progress term.
At most one transfer is in flight; the FSMs are in IDLE only between transfers.
The request bundle and the response bundle change only while the handshake is not in the phase in which the other domain may load them (REQ-HS-002).
The two-phase request and acknowledge bits are equal when no transfer is in flight; the four-phase bits are both 0.
PREADY of the requester side is high only in state RESP, one cycle per transfer.
A completer-side PSEL is high only in states SETUP and ACCESS.
Every flip-flop that drives an APB output is reset to 0.

The bridge follows AMBA APB Issue D (REF-001) on both interfaces.
The statements below restate the rules of REF-001 that the bridge relies on, with their sections.
Phases (REF-001 4.1, Figure 4-1).
A transfer starts with the Setup phase (PSEL high, PENABLE low, one cycle), then the Access phase (PENABLE high), which ends in the cycle where PREADY is high.
After PREADY the bus returns to IDLE or goes directly to the Setup phase of the next transfer.
Validity (REF-001 Appendix A).
PADDR, PPROT, PENABLE, PWRITE, PAUSER, PSTRB and the active lanes of PWDATA (and PWUSER of a write) are valid whenever PSEL is high, so the bridge captures them in the Setup cycle.
PREADY is valid when PSEL and PENABLE are high.
PRDATA of a read, PSLVERR, PRUSER of a read and PBUSER are valid when PSEL, PENABLE and PREADY are high.
Stability (REF-001 3.1, 4.1).
PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PAUSER, PWUSER do not change between the Setup and the Access phase and while PREADY is low.
The bridge relies on this only for the Setup cycle of the requester side; it guarantees it on the completer side by loading the fields into reg_apb_payload once.
Wait states (REF-001 3.1).
The completer extends the Access phase by driving PREADY low; the bridge propagates this by raising the requester-side PREADY only after the completer-side PREADY.
Error (REF-001 3.4).
PSLVERR is valid only in the last cycle of a transfer.

A transfer with an error may or may not have changed the completer; a read with an error can return invalid data and the requester may still use it, so the bridge forwards PRDATA and PSLVERR together without masking.
Strobes (REF-001 3.2).
PSTRB must be low in a read.
The bridge forwards PSTRB as received (DEC-028).
Wake-up (REF-001 3.6, APB5 only).

PWAKEUP is synchronous to its clock and shall be glitch-free to be sampled asynchronously; it may be asserted before, during or after PSEL, shall stay high until PREADY when high in the same cycle as PSEL, and should be asserted one cycle before PSEL.
A completer may wait for PWAKEUP before PREADY.
User signals (REF-001 3.7, APB5 only).
PAUSER and PWUSER are valid with PSEL (PWUSER also with PWRITE) and keep their value through the Setup and Access phases; PRUSER and PBUSER are valid in the PREADY cycle.
A signal whose width is 0 is not present.
A domain-crossing bridge should provide all user signals.

The two FSMs follow the three-process style of REF-003 with the names reg_fsm_hs_current_state and w_fsm_hs_nxt_state and the members ENUM_ST_*.
All four encodings of each 2-bit FSM are used, so there is no unused encoding; CLOSE (mst) and REQ0 (slv) are reached only with the four-phase handshake.
Requester-side FSM (m_vlsit_apbcdc_mst):

Mode/state: ENUM_ST_IDLE; Entry condition: Reset, or the end of RESP; Behavior: Waits for the Setup phase; Exit condition: i_apb_psel high and i_apb_penable low: WAIT; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: reg_req_payload loaded, reg_req toggled (two-phase) or set (four-phase)

Mode/state: ENUM_ST_WAIT; Entry condition: Request launched; Behavior: Waits for the acknowledge event: two-phase, synchronized acknowledge equal to reg_req; four-phase, synchronized acknowledge high; Exit condition: Two-phase: event, load the response output registers, raise o_apb_pready: RESP. Four-phase: event, clear reg_req: CLOSE; Outputs / side effects: o_apb_pready 0

Mode/state: ENUM_ST_CLOSE; Entry condition: Four-phase, acknowledge seen; Behavior: Waits for the synchronized acknowledge to fall; Exit condition: Acknowledge low: load the response output registers, raise o_apb_pready: RESP; Outputs / side effects: reg_req 0

Mode/state: ENUM_ST_RESP; Entry condition: Response loaded; Behavior: o_apb_pready is high for this cycle; Exit condition: Always: IDLE; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: o_apb_pready and o_apb_pslverr cleared
Completer-side FSM (m_vlsit_apbcdc_slv):

Mode/state: ENUM_ST_IDLE; Entry condition: Reset, or the end of a transfer; Behavior: Waits for the request event: two-phase, synchronized request different from reg_ack; four-phase, synchronized request high; Exit condition: Event: SETUP; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: reg_apb_payload loaded from the request bundle, o_apb_psel high
Mode/state: ENUM_ST_SETUP; Entry condition: Request loaded; Behavior: Setup phase, o_apb_penable low; Exit condition: Always: ACCESS; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: o_apb_penable high

Mode/state: ENUM_ST_ACCESS; Entry condition: Setup phase done; Behavior: Access phase; waits for i_apb_pready; Exit condition: i_apb_pready high: two-phase IDLE, four-phase REQ0; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: reg_resp_hold loaded, o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable low, reg_ack toggled (two-phase) or set (four-phase)

Mode/state: ENUM_ST_REQ0; Entry condition: Four-phase, acknowledge launched; Behavior: Waits for the synchronized request to fall; Exit condition: Request low: IDLE; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: reg_ack cleared

There is no arbitration: one requester-side interface and one completer-side interface, one transfer at a time (DEC-013).
There is no buffering other than the four registers of the two bundles.
A new Setup phase that the requester drives before PREADY cannot occur (APB is non-pipelined).
Latency.
Let N be the number of synchronizer stages, T_mst and T_slv the clock periods, w the number of completer wait states.
The duration D is measured from the first cycle of the Setup phase to the end of the PREADY cycle on the requester side.

From the structure (the request needs up to N + 1 slv edges to be loaded, two slv cycles for Setup and Access plus w wait cycles, the acknowledge needs up to N + 1 mst edges, plus the Setup and PREADY cycles) the bounds are:
Handshake: Two-phase; Upper bound of D: (N + 3) x T_mst + (N + 3 + w) x T_slv; Equal clocks, N stages, w wait states: 2N + 6 + w cycles
Handshake: Four-phase; Upper bound of D: (2N + 4) x T_mst + (2N + 4 + w) x T_slv; Equal clocks, N stages, w wait states: 4N + 8 + w cycles

The prototype was measured for both handshakes, N = 2, 3, 4, eight clock ratios (1:1, 1:3, 3:1, 3:7, 7:3, 1:2, 2:1, 4:5), and w = 0 and 2, one starting phase per ratio: 96 cases, no case above the bound (waveforms/apbcdc_latency_table.txt, produced by waveforms/proto/latency_sweep.py).
For equal clocks the measured value equals the formula in every case.
The bound is derived by analysis and checked against one starting phase per ratio, not against every phase; TEST-018 repeats the check on the RTL for several phases.

Throughput.
One transfer per D; no pipelining.
The two-phase handshake is the faster; the four-phase handshake costs about 6 more cycles at N = 2 for equal clocks.
Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-25): the IP contains no memory or macro; the only storage is the registers of the two bundles and the control flip-flops (Section 5.1).
Nothing is held when no transfer is in progress except the last bundle values, which have no meaning.

Block-level simulation with scoreboards, directed tests for each operation, constrained-random traffic over many clock ratios, protocol assertions on both interfaces, structural and timing reviews of the crossings.

The environment drives the two clocks from independent generators with random ratio and phase, runs the synchronizer simulation model with random extra latency (REQ-RTL-002), and models the requester and the completer with the rules of REF-001 (wait states, errors, back-to-back, idle gaps).
The scoreboard compares both interfaces transfer by transfer (REQ-FUNC-001 to REQ-FUNC-003).

Evidence from the prototype (not from the delivered RTL, which does not exist yet): the prototype waveforms/proto/apbcdc_proto.sv follows this specification. waveforms/proto/regress.py ran 80 simulations (two handshake types, two synchronizer depths, APB4 and APB5, ten clock ratios from 1:1 to 9:1 and 1:9) of 40 random transfers each (3200 transfers) with random wait states (0 to 6), errors, idle gaps and back-to-back traffic, checking every transfer on both interfaces: 0 failures (waveforms/apbcdc_random_regression.txt).

Injecting a lost PSLVERR and an inverted two-phase event condition made the regression fail (2 of 2 injected faults caught). waveforms/proto/latency_sweep.py produced the latency table of Section 10.4.

The prototype synchronizer has no metastability model, and the prototype tests did not include reset in the middle of random traffic (shown only by WF-012) or the APB protocol assertions; these shall be verified on the RTL.

Evidence from the delivered RTL (rtl/, written 2026-10-25, rule check PASS, slang lint 0 errors, Verilator lint 0 errors and four warnings for the unused user ports of the default APB4 configuration): verification/vlsit_run_sim.py quick ran the testbench verification/tb_apbcdc.sv (28 assertions on both APB interfaces and the bridge, with hit counts, plus a two-sided scoreboard) for 16 configurations (both handshakes, APB4 and APB5, clock ratios 1:1, 1:3, 3:1 and 9:1), each in the synthesis branch and in the simulation branch with the metastability model for the seeds 1, 2 and 3: 64 runs, 0 failures, every run prints assertion failures: 0, assertions never exercised: 0 (verification/logs/, verification/quick_run.txt).

Every third configuration has a requester that changes the fields in the Access phase (checking that the Setup values are used, ERR-004) and every third APB5 configuration has a requester that never drives PWAKEUP (checking REQ-APB5-001). verification/vlsit_gen_sim_waves.py simulated the 12 waveforms of the plan on the RTL: all 12 are MATCH (the WaveJSON of the RTL, internal rows included, equals the WaveJSON of the figure) and the assertions pass in the metastability branch for each scenario (verification/waveforms_sim/, index waveform_compare.md, checked by vlsit_sim_evidence.py check).

A fault injection into a copy of the RTL (8 faults of the control and the handshake) was caught by an assertion in 7 cases; the eighth (the completer side loading its request register in every cycle instead of at the request event) is equivalent in simulation, because the hold register is stable, and is a timing property that only the structural check (TEST-015) and the SDC (TEST-016) can show.

The clock ratios beyond the quick set, the latency bound for many starting phases (TEST-018), the structural check, the SDC in a sign-off tool and a reset in the middle of random traffic (shown only by WF-012) are not yet verified on the RTL.

This subsection answers the question of the designer of 2026-10-25 and corrects an earlier statement of the author: -datapath_only is the Vivado (XDC) option and -ignore_clock_latency is the Synopsys option of the same purpose; the SDC of this IP uses the Synopsys form (DEC-007).
The reasoning below is the author's analysis; the tool semantics shall be confirmed in the Synopsys documentation (OI-004).
Why a bound and not a false path.
The bridge relies on an ordering in time: the bundle must be stable at the destination flop before the control bit, which crossed through N synchronizer stages, tells the destination FSM to load it.
A false path or an asynchronous clock group removes every check from the bundle path, so place and route may route it arbitrarily long and the ordering is broken without a warning.
A bound on the data-path delay keeps the ordering true by construction (UG903, Constraining Asynchronous Signals, makes the same case for buses that are not Gray coded).
Why the default check is meaningless.

For two unrelated clocks the setup relationship is derived from the nearest launch and capture edges, which depend on a phase that is not fixed; the result is an arbitrary budget. set_max_delay replaces it by an absolute delay, independent of the edges.
Why the clock latency is ignored.
By default the tool counts the clock network latency and uncertainty in the budget.

The two clock trees are independent, so their latency difference has no fixed value and changes after clock-tree synthesis; counting it would add or remove an arbitrary amount. -ignore_clock_latency (Synopsys) or -datapath_only (Vivado) leaves only the data-path delay: clock-to-Q, logic, wire and setup of the destination, a physical quantity that can be controlled and repeated.
Why (N - 1) x T_dst.

The destination FSM sees the control event after the control bit has passed N stages, that is at the destination edge number N after the first edge that samples it, and loads the bundle at the next edge.

In the worst case the first edge samples the bit right after launch, so the bundle has at least N destination periods; the budget (N - 1) x T_dst leaves one destination period as a guard band for what the option removed (clock latency difference, uncertainty) and for the setup time.
REQ-TIM-003 requires the post-CTS latency difference to stay below that guard band.
Why no hold check.
A hold check between unrelated clocks compares edges with no fixed relation.
The functional hold is guaranteed by the protocol: the bundle does not change until the handshake has completed. set_false_path -hold removes the meaningless check; the setup bound stays.
Why no bus-skew constraint. set_bus_skew is for buses that the destination samples at an unknown time (for example Gray pointers).
The bundles here are loaded only after the control event, so all bits only need to arrive before the load, which the maximum delay guarantees.
The control bits are single bits.
Why no clock group.

UG903 states that a clock group or a false path on the same paths makes the maximum-delay constraints ineffective; the SDC of this IP therefore leaves the clocks unrelated and covers every crossing by an exception, so that any other path between the domains is reported with the default relation and is found as a design error.
Synchronizer depth.

The SDC takes the depth N as a variable and refuses N below 2: the value PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE = 0 has no stage, the bundle would have at most one destination period and the budget formula would give 0 or less.

PREADY on the requester-side interface shall be low from the Setup phase until the response is available, and shall then be high for exactly one cycle of i_clk_mst, in a cycle in which PSEL and PENABLE are high.

On the completer-side interface the bridge shall drive PSEL high for the whole transfer, PENABLE low in the Setup cycle and high from the next cycle until the transfer completes, keep PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PAUSER, PWUSER unchanged from the Setup phase until PREADY is seen high, and drive PSEL and PENABLE low when no transfer is in progress.

PPROT and PSTRB shall be forwarded unchanged. The bridge does not check the rule that PSTRB is low in a read; it forwards what the requester drove.
The IP shall expose exactly the ports of Section 6.2 of the configured revision.
Every output of both APB interfaces shall be the output of a flip-flop with no logic after it, so that it is glitch-free (REF-001 3.6 requires this for PWAKEUP).
Structural check of the RTL and the netlist: TEST-015
Outputs that need not be valid shall hold a stable value (reset value zero). PRDATA, PRUSER, PBUSER are valid with PREADY; PSLVERR is low when PREADY is low.

PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE = 0 selects the two-phase handshake: the request bit toggles once per transfer and the acknowledge bit toggles once per transfer. PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE = 1 selects the four-phase handshake: request high, acknowledge high, request low, acknowledge low. The function seen on the two APB interfaces shall be the same.
Simulation: TEST-002, TEST-008; assertions SVA-012, SVA-013; waveform WF-001, WF-007

The request bundle in the requester-side hold register shall not change from the edge that launches the request until the acknowledge was seen, and the response bundle in the completer-side hold register shall not change from the edge that launches the acknowledge until the next request was seen.

The request bit shall be launched at the same clock edge at which the request bundle is loaded, and the acknowledge bit at the same edge at which the response bundle is loaded; between a launch flip-flop and its synchronizer there shall be no logic.
Structural check: TEST-015; STA review: TEST-016
With the four-phase handshake the requester side shall raise PREADY only after the acknowledge returned to 0, so that the handshake is closed before the next Setup phase can be accepted.
Simulation: TEST-008; assertion SVA-013; waveform WF-007
The IP shall be correct for any frequency ratio and any phase of i_clk_mst and i_clk_slv, equal frequency included.

Only the five crossings of Section 7.2 shall exist between the domains: request, request bundle, acknowledge, response bundle, and wake-up. Each control bit shall cross through a synchronizer and no bundle bit shall cross through one.

The synchronizer depth shall follow PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE (1 and 2: two stages, 3: three stages, 4: four stages). The value 0 (no stage) is for simulation only and shall not be used in a netlist; the SDC rejects it.
Elaboration and SDC check: TEST-014, TEST-016

Both resets shall be active-low with asynchronous assertion. While one is asserted, every flip-flop of its domain shall be at its reset value: all payload registers 0, request 0, acknowledge 0, both FSMs in IDLE, PSEL, PENABLE, PREADY, PSLVERR, PWAKEUP 0.

The two resets shall be asserted together and each shall be released synchronously to the clock of its domain, outside the IP. A transfer in flight when a reset is asserted is lost. Asserting only one reset is not supported.

In APB5, o_apb_pwakeup shall be a flip-flop output that is high whenever the synchronized i_apb_pwakeup is high or a transfer is in progress on the completer side, and shall be high no later than o_apb_psel.
Simulation: TEST-009; assertions SVA-014, SVA-015; waveform WF-009
In APB5, PAUSER, PWUSER, PRUSER, PBUSER shall be transported with the same timing rules as the other request and response fields; a signal whose width parameter is 0 is not present.
With PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 0 the APB5 signals shall have no effect: o_apb_pwakeup is 0 and the user outputs are 0.
The IP shall accept the parameter values of Section 8. The behavior with an illegal value is not specified and the IP does not check it.
Elaboration of the legal extremes: TEST-014

With the two-phase handshake, the duration from the first cycle of the Setup phase to the end of the PREADY cycle on the requester side shall not exceed (N + 3) x T_mst + (N + 3 + w) x T_slv, where N is the number of synchronizer stages, w the number of completer wait states, and T the clock periods.
Latency sweep: TEST-018; waveform WF-001, WF-010, WF-011
With the four-phase handshake the same duration shall not exceed (2N + 4) x T_mst + (2N + 4 + w) x T_slv.
The bridge shall carry one transfer at a time and shall accept the next Setup phase in the cycle after the PREADY cycle.

The IP shall be delivered with an SDC file in the Synopsys dialect that defines the two clocks, the interface budgets, and the exceptions of the five crossings, with the budgets computed from the clock periods and the synchronizer depth.

Each crossing path shall be constrained by set_max_delay with the clock latency ignored; no set_clock_groups -asynchronous and no set_false_path (other than the hold-only false path of the crossings) shall exist between the two clocks.

The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and shall use the hierarchy of Section 14.2.

The synchronizer cells shall be instantiated only inside the wrapper m_vlsit_apbcdc_cell_sync of 000_Common/rtl_lib, named u_dont_touch_ followed by the function (REF-003 NAM-09), with a simulation model that adds a random extra latency of 0, 1 or 2 destination cycles to the output.

The random regression shall cover both handshake types, two synchronizer depths, APB4 and APB5, and at least ten clock ratios including equal clocks and a ratio of 9 to 1 in both directions, with wait states and errors, and shall report no error.
